key_insight: IMPACT combines inverter-level cloud dynamics with solar geometry and weather inputs to improve 10–110-minute-ahead probabilistic photovoltaic power forecasts.
engineering_relevance: More accurate, calibrated short-term solar forecasts could support grid balancing, storage scheduling, and photovoltaic plant operations.
method: Fuse four branches for plant history, inverter dynamics, future solar geometry, and current weather using gated cross-attention.
Encode inverter dynamics with learned-adjacency graph attention and add horizon-weighted cloud heterogeneity and ramp-down signals.
Learn horizon-conditioned corrections to smart persistence, then calibrate quantile forecasts online with kernel-weighted adaptive conformal calibration.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports outperforming all 14 baselines with FSS 0.2950, a 0.099 advantage over the runner-up; ablations support every branch, with FSS 0.198 under overcast skies and 0.255 under variable skies.
watch_item: The abstract does not specify dataset scale or cross-site validation, leaving generalization to other photovoltaic plants uncertain.
paper_title: IMPACT: Inverter-Informed Multimodal Learning for Photovoltaic Generation Forecasting
